target_customer: Informal-sector transport operators, passengers, merchants and institutions in Nigeria/Africa
problem: Cash-based micro-transactions (e.g. bus fares) in Africa's informal sector are untracked and leak revenue.
business_model: Transaction commission: 3% on each processed fare transaction, with TAP funding top-up points and card readers (How We Made It in Africa, 2023)

founders.name: Michael Oluwole
founders.background_notes: Mechanical engineering, business process development and project management per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Offline-capable NFC card, validators, top-up network and settlement; standard payments engineering plus hardware deployment and government integration.

defensibility.rationale: Won the Lagos BRT contract against several European bidders, and card base plus installed validators give lock-in with transit authorities; government contracts can be rebid.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Several European firms bid for the Lagos BRT contract and TAP won it in 2020; no incumbent copy or acquisition found.

market_need_then: Informal and government buses in Lagos handled cash fares; the CEO cites about 300,000 daily riders on government buses and an estimated 7 million daily danfo passengers as the opportunity, and 64 million Nigerian adults lacking bank access per one outlet.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: Making life easier for africans one TAP at a time

branding.brand_signature: The Cowry card, the product name used by riders more than the company name.
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the card rollout in Lagos transit, but no sourced meme, merch or community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: The Cowry card is used by nearly five million people per the CEO and is the public face, but no sourced press on the brand itself or visual identity.

pivots.from: Earlier startup ideas from university days (idea from 2013)
pivots.why: Founders pivoted into transportation; Lagos government contract in 2020 was the turning point.

outcome_analysis: Touch and Pay turned a 2019 pivot into transport fare payments into the Cowry card, winning the Lagos BRT contract in 2020 and growing from one million to nearly five million users by 2024 with over 20 billion naira processed, and says it is profitable. Outside funding is murky: Crunchbase-based reports cite $4 million from Unicorn Growth Capital and a stalled 2023 raise, so government dependence and a thin funding record are the main risks.
notes: Directory Active, consistent. Funding is unverified so no round is recorded: Condia (2024-10) and TechCabal cite $4M from Unicorn Growth Capital via Crunchbase data, undated; Seedtable cites TechBuild Africa for a $3M seed dated 2022-09 (not fetched); the 2022-11 Ecobank Fintech Challenge $50K prize is reported second-hand. How We Made It in Africa (2023-06) says early funding was from founders, family and friends and the CEO was then raising $10M; Condia says a planned $4M 2023 raise stalled. Founding year conflicts: TechCabal 2017, Extruct 2019, idea in 2013 per the founder; 2019 kept from the transport pivot. Profitability is a founder claim. TechCabal returned 403 on fetch, so its content rests on search summaries. Dated competitors not found (European BRT bidders unnamed), list empty. The Cowry name origin is not stated in any source; the cowry shell link remains unclaimed. Founder education and priors only from earlier record. Completeness pass: the 3M seed (2022-09) is reported by Disrupt Africa, WeeTracker and TechBuild Africa (investor list from Seedtable; Tekedia Capital also named elsewhere). The 50K grant rests on Startuplist only (dated 2022-10-28; earlier note said the Ecobank prize was 2022-11). Condia reports 4M total (Crunchbase, undated), larger than the recorded rounds; the gap is unresolved and not summed. CB Insights reports 3.55M over 7 rounds.
